newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian government coalition falls apart.
newsitem.headline: Estonian government coalition falls apart.

text.p: The one-year-old coalition government of the Baltic state of Estonia fell apart on Thursday, plunging the small country into political crisis.
The coalition collapsed as junior partner the Reform Party announced it could no longer rule with main government group, the Coalition Party.
The Reformists walked out in anger at a pact signed by Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi, Coalition Party head, with the leading opposition party.
"We have taken the vote to leave the government," a spokesman for the Reform Party said.

Estonia has been plagued by political instability since quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991. The government of Vaehi's Coalition Party and the Reformists was the sixth since independence was regained.
The spokesman said the vote to leave the government was overwhelming at 59 for and just eight against. It came after nearly three hours of talks among the party council.
But Estonia, the smallest of the three Baltic states, has kept on the path of reform despite political turbulence and is viewed as one of the most successful of the ex-Communist states.
The government also includes a smaller bloc of rural parties.
The Reform Party was furious with Vaehi for concluding a cooperation deal with leading opposition party, the Centre Party, and demanded that he scrap it.
The Reformists said the deal would change Estonia's foreign policy and bring it closer to huge neighbour Russia, which many Estonians fear wants to reassert its influence over them.

Russia ruled Estonia and fellow Baltic states Latvia and Lithuania for most of the last 200 years and all three look with bitterness on the 50 years during which they lived as unwilling Soviet citizens.
Vaehi refused to comply with the Reform Party's demands and tried to persuade his coalition colleagues to stay in the government.
Many observers expect the Coalition Party to try and form a government with the Centre Party, a rerun of the previous government.
That administration collapsed amid scandal after the Centre Party leader was found to have taped confidential recordings of conversations with leading politicians.
